response.rationale: C1 is the most composite diagnosis: long-standing childhood nyctalopia, flat rod ERG, progressive amplitude loss, inferonasal field defect, and complete outer-retinal/RPE loss all support retinitis pigmentosa, while the explicit absence of pigmentary degeneration and the presence of only yellow spots require an atypical subtype. R1 explains some RPE/outer-retinal loss but would need choroidal/choriocapillaris blindness and X-linked findings, which are absent. R4 is less complete because it omits the atypical modifier, and R3 is weakened by normal chromatic and acuity preservation and a predominantly rod-based phenotype.

rejected.why: Choroidal dystrophy is too nonspecific and the evidence item with yellow spots and hypofluorescence cannot explain the flat rod ERG and inferonasal field defect.
Cone-rod dystrophy is contradicted by primary night blindness, flat rod ERG, preserved color/vision, and central macula with normal acuity.

The evidence supports RP, but the classic label is missing the essential atypical feature: no pigmentary degeneration. R4 is intentionally refined by C1's atypical completion, so R4 alone is less precise.
